questions.q: Which pharyngeal arch fails to form or regresses in the human embryo?
questions.explain: In humans the arches are numbered 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 because the fifth never forms or is rudimentary.

open.q: Which pharyngeal arch fails to form or regresses in the human embryo?
accept: Rudimentary arch between the fourth and sixth

questions.q: Which cranial nerve supplies the muscles of mastication that develop from the first pharyngeal arch?
questions.explain: The mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve supplies first arch muscles such as masseter, temporalis and the pterygoids.

open.q: Which cranial nerve supplies the muscles of mastication that develop from the first pharyngeal arch?
accept: Mandibular division of the fifth cranial nerve

questions.q: Which cranial nerve supplies the muscles of facial expression, which develop from the second pharyngeal arch?
questions.explain: The facial nerve is the nerve of the second (hyoid) arch, so facial palsy causes loss of facial expression.

open.q: Which cranial nerve supplies the muscles of facial expression, which develop from the second pharyngeal arch?

questions.q: Which muscle is the only one derived from the third pharyngeal arch?
questions.explain: Stylopharyngeus is supplied by the glossopharyngeal nerve. Buccinator and the posterior belly of digastric come from the second arch, and the anterior belly from the first.

open.q: Which muscle is the only one derived from the third pharyngeal arch?
accept: Muscle supplied by the glossopharyngeal nerve
Only muscle supplied by CN IX in the pharynx

questions.q: Meckel cartilage is a derivative of which pharyngeal arch?
questions.explain: Meckel cartilage is the cartilage of the first (mandibular) arch. It forms the malleus and incus, and the mandible ossifies around it.

open.q: Meckel cartilage is a derivative of which pharyngeal arch?

questions.q: Which middle ear bone develops from the cartilage of the second pharyngeal arch?
questions.explain: Reichert cartilage of the second arch forms the stapes, the styloid process and the lesser horn and upper body of the hyoid. The malleus and incus come from the first arch.

open.q: Which middle ear bone develops from the cartilage of the second pharyngeal arch?

questions.q: From which pharyngeal pouch does the epithelial lining of the palatine tonsil develop?
questions.explain: The second pouch epithelium forms the lining of the tonsillar fossa and the crypts of the palatine tonsil, which are infiltrated by lymphoid tissue later.

open.q: From which pharyngeal pouch does the epithelial lining of the palatine tonsil develop?

questions.q: Which pharyngeal pouch gives rise to the thymus and the inferior parathyroid glands?
questions.explain: The dorsal wing of the third pouch forms the inferior parathyroid and the ventral wing forms the thymus. The superior parathyroid comes from the fourth pouch.

open.q: Which pharyngeal pouch gives rise to the thymus and the inferior parathyroid glands?

questions.q: From which pharyngeal pouch do the superior parathyroid glands develop?
questions.explain: The dorsal wing of the fourth pouch forms the superior parathyroid gland. It migrates less than the inferior gland, so it ends up higher on the thyroid.

open.q: From which pharyngeal pouch do the superior parathyroid glands develop?

questions.q: Which structure develops from the first pharyngeal pouch?
questions.explain: The first pouch expands into the tubotympanic recess, which forms the middle ear cavity, mastoid antrum and auditory tube.

open.q: Which recess formed by the first pharyngeal pouch gives rise to the middle ear cavity and auditory tube?
accept: Eustachian tube and middle ear precursor

questions.q: Which pharyngeal cleft persists as the external acoustic meatus?
questions.explain: The first cleft deepens into the external acoustic meatus. The tympanic membrane forms where it meets the first pouch.

open.q: Which pharyngeal cleft persists as the external acoustic meatus?

questions.q: Which pharyngeal arch overgrows the second to fourth clefts, forming a temporary cavity called the cervical sinus?
questions.explain: The second arch grows caudally over the lower arches and fuses with the neck wall. This buries the clefts in the cervical sinus, which normally disappears.

open.q: Which pharyngeal arch overgrows the second to fourth clefts, forming a temporary cavity called the cervical sinus?

questions.q: A young adult has a painless cystic swelling along the anterior border of sternocleidomastoid. Which embryological remnant is the most likely cause?
questions.explain: A branchial cyst arises from remnants of the cervical sinus, which forms when the second arch overgrows the lower clefts. A thyroglossal cyst is in the midline.

open.q: A young adult has a painless cystic swelling along the anterior border of sternocleidomastoid. Which embryological remnant is the most likely cause?

questions.q: A newborn has hypocalcaemic seizures, a cleft palate, cardiac outflow defects and an absent thymus on imaging. Which pair of pharyngeal pouches developed abnormally?
questions.explain: DiGeorge syndrome (22q11 deletion) causes hypoplasia of the third and fourth pouch derivatives. The thymus and parathyroids are lost, giving T cell deficiency and hypocalcaemia.

open.q: A newborn has hypocalcaemic seizures, a cleft palate, cardiac outflow defects and an absent thymus on imaging. Which pair of pharyngeal pouches developed abnormally?

questions.q: Which prominence forms the forehead and the bridge of the nose?
questions.explain: The frontonasal prominence lies above the stomodeum and forms the forehead and nasal bridge. The nasal placodes later split it into medial and lateral nasal prominences.

open.q: Which prominence forms the forehead and the bridge of the nose?

questions.q: Which pair of prominences merge to form the intermaxillary segment, including the philtrum of the upper lip?
questions.explain: The medial nasal prominences fuse in the midline to form the intermaxillary segment, which gives the philtrum, the premaxillary part of the maxilla and the primary palate.

open.q: Which pair of prominences merge to form the intermaxillary segment, including the philtrum of the upper lip?

questions.q: Failure of fusion between which structures causes a unilateral cleft lip?
questions.explain: Cleft lip results from failure of the maxillary prominence to fuse with the merged medial nasal prominences. The defect lies to one side of the philtrum.

open.q: Failure of fusion between which two embryonic structures causes a unilateral cleft lip?
accept: Medial nasal prominence and maxillary prominence

questions.q: A child has a small mandible, downward slanting palpebral fissures and malformed external ears. Which embryonic tissue is mainly deficient?
questions.explain: Treacher Collins syndrome is caused by deficient migration of neural crest cells into the first and second arches. It gives mandibular and malar hypoplasia and ear anomalies.

open.q: A child has a small mandible, downward slanting palpebral fissures and malformed external ears. Which embryonic tissue is mainly deficient?
accept: Neural crest of the first arch
Cranial neural crest migrating to the first arch

questions.q: The maxillary prominences give rise to which parts of the face?
options: Forehead and bridge of the nose
questions.explain: The maxillary prominences form the cheeks and the lateral parts of the upper lip. The medial nasal prominences form the philtrum, and the mandibular prominences form the lower lip and chin.

open.q: Which parts of the face develop from the maxillary prominences?
accept: Lateral parts of the upper lip and cheeks
Upper cheek and upper lip sides
Upper lip lateral to the philtrum

questions.q: The primary palate develops from which structure?
questions.explain: The primary palate forms from the intermaxillary segment, which is the triangular premaxillary part of the palate in front of the incisive foramen.

open.q: The primary palate develops from which structure?

questions.q: Which structure marks the dividing point between the primary and the secondary palate?
questions.explain: The incisive foramen is the landmark between the primary palate in front and the secondary palate behind. Clefts are classified as anterior or posterior to it.

open.q: Which structure marks the dividing point between the primary and the secondary palate?

questions.q: The secondary palate forms from the fusion of which structures?
questions.explain: The palatine shelves are outgrowths of the maxillary prominences. They elevate to a horizontal position and fuse with each other and the nasal septum in the 8th to 12th weeks.

open.q: The secondary palate forms from the fusion of which structures, outgrowths of the maxillary prominences?

questions.q: A newborn has a small mandible, a posteriorly displaced tongue and a U-shaped cleft palate. What is the embryological explanation for the cleft?
questions.explain: In Pierre Robin sequence the small mandible keeps the tongue high between the palatine shelves, so they cannot elevate and fuse.

open.q: A newborn has a small mandible, a posteriorly displaced tongue and a U-shaped cleft palate. What is the embryological explanation for the cleft?
accept: Tongue positioned high between the shelves

questions.q: From which structures does the anterior two-thirds of the tongue mainly develop?
questions.explain: Two distal tongue buds (lateral lingual swellings) and the median tuberculum impar arise from the first arch and form the anterior two-thirds.

open.q: From which paired swellings of the first arch does the anterior two-thirds of the tongue mainly develop?

questions.q: Which structure forms the posterior one-third of the tongue?
questions.explain: The copula and hypobranchial eminence of the third and fourth arches overgrow the second arch, so the posterior third is supplied by the glossopharyngeal nerve.

open.q: Which structure of the third and fourth arches forms the posterior one-third of the tongue?
accept: Copula overgrown by third arch tissue

questions.q: Which nerve carries general sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue?
questions.explain: The lingual nerve, a branch of the mandibular nerve, matches the first arch origin of this part. Chorda tympani carries taste instead.

open.q: Which nerve carries general sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue?
accept: Lingual branch of the trigeminal nerve

questions.q: The intrinsic muscles of the tongue develop from which mesoderm?
questions.explain: Myoblasts migrate from the occipital somites and carry the hypoglossal nerve with them. Palatoglossus is the exception, supplied by the vagus.

open.q: The intrinsic muscles of the tongue develop from which mesoderm?
accept: Somitic mesoderm of the occipital region

questions.q: An infant has a midline neck swelling that moves upward when the tongue is protruded. Which embryological structure is responsible?
questions.explain: A thyroglossal duct cyst arises from remnants of the duct along which the thyroid descended. It is attached to the hyoid and so moves with swallowing and tongue protrusion.

open.q: An infant has a midline neck swelling that moves upward when the tongue is protruded. Which embryological structure is responsible?

questions.q: Where does the thyroid diverticulum originate in the floor of the pharynx?
questions.explain: The thyroid arises from an endodermal thickening between the tuberculum impar and the copula. This site persists as the foramen caecum.

open.q: Where does the thyroid diverticulum originate in the floor of the pharynx?

questions.q: Which thyroid cells, derived from the ultimobranchial body, secrete calcitonin?
questions.explain: The ultimobranchial body (from the fourth or fifth pouch) brings neural crest derived C cells into the thyroid. Follicular cells make thyroxine and triiodothyronine.

open.q: Which thyroid cells, derived from the ultimobranchial body, secrete calcitonin?
